## Native consequences change carrier formation

The [next source-grounded continuation](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSEQUENCE-RECONSTRUCTION-INTEGRATION.md) finds a positive reconstruction mechanism within the unchanged native law. Captured local support can produce an A template. After the previous resident disappears, free template abundance enters the competing association rates. The retained product changes which carrier forms; that carrier then determines which local copying reaction and immediate repair response can occur. This is one continuing material history, with no additional reward, selector recipe or source conversion.

Four possible histories start at the actual installed acquisition checkpoint. Copying and local loss consume equal support, while only copying adds the template that mediates the later association difference. Both A and H associations remain possible and are followed into their actual responses. Exact full-channel probabilities and an independently reviewed hand deduction establish an immediate formation bias under the specified law. They do not establish eventual retention, useful adaptation in every context or ethical priority.

The alternative reached carrier states can have identical total A/H counts, support, expenditure and learned apparatus while permitting different local transitions. Omitting resident placement therefore fails one exact Markov projection; an adequate representation must preserve that relation or sufficient history. The branch thus constrains the core's articulation: how constituents are organized can matter beyond their totals, and activity can change the conditions of later organization.

The acquired reader remains a distinct fixed relation in these same states. Native carrier reconstruction does not reopen its records or derive a learned revision rule. Existing selector/updater, architecture and method formation already supply stronger conditional revisions under other laws. The remaining explanation connects actual physical formation and retained consequences to context-sensitive revision of the relation maintained, and to the warranted significance of that revision within the whole.
